## Lee — worth getting our own dumper?

I reckon it’s worth us going halves on a secondhand tracked dumper rather than paying to hire one every time we’ve got a bigger job. We’ve worked together long enough to know it’ll get used, but here’s the money side written down.

**What we’re spending now**

We hired the tracked dumper from Sittingbourne for 14 days this year at £85 a day. That’s £1,190 just in day hire, then £30 delivery each time. Roughly £1,600 all in over the year, and nothing to show for it afterwards.

**What this one would cost**

There’s a bloke in Faversham selling a 2019 500kg tracked dumper for **£1,650 ono — £825 each** at the asking price. He says it had new tracks last spring, so we’d want to check those and see it working before agreeing anything.

At this year’s hire spend, the purchase price is covered in about a year. Even at half that use, it’s about two years. That’s before servicing and repairs, obviously — I’m not pretending an older machine won’t need money spending on it.

We’ve already got three patio digs and the Boughton drive booked for spring, so there’s work lined up for it.

**It’s not just the hire bill**

When they didn’t have one in September, we barrowed six tonnes of muck at Hernhill. That cost us two extra days, and your back was gone for a week. Then there was the delivery that turned up at 11 and cost us half the morning. Having our own means we can load it up and get on.

**How we’d split it**

- Buy it 50/50.
- Keep it under cover in my lean-to at the yard.
- Split servicing and normal wear-and-tear repairs 50/50.
- Fuel goes against whichever job it’s being used on.
- Whoever breaks it through misuse pays for that repair.

If it doesn’t work out, we can sell it on. They seem to hold their value, though we can’t guarantee getting every penny back.

Come and look at it with me this Saturday, before someone else has it. No commitment till we’ve both had a proper look — after 15 years, you know I’d rather we were both happy with it.
